fixIt.text: She go to the market yesterday.
fixIt.explain: Yesterday is finished time, so use the past simple: went.

fixIt.text: We buy a new fan last week.
fixIt.explain: Last week is finished time: bought.

fixIt.text: Be quiet, my mother cooking dinner now.
fixIt.explain: Now needs the present continuous: is + -ing.

fixIt.text: He going to school by bike every day.
fixIt.explain: Every day is a habit, so use the present simple: goes.

fixIt.text: I see that film two weeks ago.
fixIt.explain: Ago tells you it is the past: saw.

fixIt.text: When I arrived, they eat dinner.
fixIt.explain: An action in progress in the past: were eating.

fixIt.text: Look at the clouds. It go to rain.
fixIt.explain: A prediction from what you can see: be going to.

fixIt.text: Did you went to the party on Saturday?
fixIt.explain: After did, use the base form: Did you go?

fixIt.text: I didn't saw him at work today.
fixIt.explain: After didn't, use the base form: didn't see.

fixIt.text: I have never eat durian.
fixIt.explain: Present perfect is have + past participle: have eaten.

fixIt.text: She lives here since 2020.
fixIt.explain: With since and a starting point, use the present perfect: has lived.

fixIt.text: My brother born in 2005.
fixIt.explain: Birth is in the past: was born.

fixIt.text: My father work in a bank.
fixIt.explain: He, she or it in the present simple: add -s. My father works.

fixIt.text: She like spicy food.
fixIt.explain: She likes: add -s after he, she or it.

fixIt.text: He don't speak French.
fixIt.explain: He, she or it takes doesn't, not don't.

fixIt.text: My sister have two children.
fixIt.explain: He, she or it: has, not have.

fixIt.text: Does she likes coffee?
fixIt.explain: The -s moves to does, so the verb has no -s: Does she like?

fixIt.text: Dara watch the news every evening.
fixIt.explain: Verbs ending in -ch add -es: watches.

fixIt.text: Sophea study English at ACE.
fixIt.explain: Consonant + y becomes -ies: studies.

fixIt.text: I have two brother and one sister.
fixIt.explain: Two means more than one, so add -s: brothers.

fixIt.text: There are many book on the table.
fixIt.explain: Many + plural noun: many books.

fixIt.text: Their three childs go to the same school.
fixIt.explain: Child has an irregular plural: children.

fixIt.text: How many peoples came to the wedding?
fixIt.explain: People is already plural.

fixIt.text: She gave me some good advices.
fixIt.explain: Advice is uncountable, so it never takes -s.

fixIt.text: Siem Reap is one of the biggest city in Cambodia.
fixIt.explain: One of the + plural noun: one of the biggest cities.

fixIt.text: This is my friend car.
fixIt.explain: To show who owns something, add 's: my friend's car.

fixIt.text: What is your teacher name?
fixIt.explain: The name belongs to the teacher: your teacher's name.

fixIt.text: My sister bag is red.
fixIt.explain: The bag belongs to my sister: my sister's bag.

fixIt.text: My mother is teacher.
fixIt.explain: Jobs need a or an: She is a teacher.

fixIt.text: I eat a apple every morning.
fixIt.explain: Use an before a vowel sound: an apple.

fixIt.text: Sun rises in the east.
fixIt.explain: There is only one sun, so use the: the sun.

fixIt.text: Do you have car?
fixIt.explain: One car you don't know yet: a car.

fixIt.text: We waited for a hour.
fixIt.explain: The h in hour is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound: an hour.

fixIt.text: She goes to an university in Siem Reap.
fixIt.explain: University starts with a "you" sound: a university.

fixIt.text: He is best student in our class.
fixIt.explain: Superlatives need the: the best.

fixIt.text: I have class in Monday.
fixIt.explain: Days take on: on Monday.

fixIt.text: The film starts on 7 o'clock.
fixIt.explain: Clock times take at: at 7 o'clock.

fixIt.text: I came to Phnom Penh at 2019.
fixIt.explain: Years take in: in 2019.

fixIt.text: We went at the beach on Sunday.
fixIt.explain: Movement towards a place: go to.

fixIt.text: I like listening music.
fixIt.explain: You listen to something: listening to music.

fixIt.text: She is married with a doctor.
fixIt.explain: You are married to someone.

fixIt.text: It depends of the weather.
fixIt.explain: It depends on something.

fixIt.text: We arrived to the airport at 6.
fixIt.explain: Arrive at a building or place, arrive in a city. Never arrive to.

fixIt.text: Last night I watch a film with my sister.
fixIt.explain: Last night is finished time: watched.

fixIt.text: She is cook rice in the kitchen right now.
fixIt.explain: Right now: is + -ing, is cooking.

fixIt.text: We was very tired after the trip.
fixIt.explain: We, you and they take were.

fixIt.text: Did she finished her homework?
fixIt.explain: After did, use the base form: Did she finish?

fixIt.text: I am going to visiting my grandparents next week.
fixIt.explain: Going to + base form: going to visit.

fixIt.text: I was eat dinner when the phone rang.
fixIt.explain: In progress when something happened: was + -ing.

fixIt.text: I have already see that film.
fixIt.explain: Have + past participle: have seen, not have saw.

fixIt.text: I promise I call you tonight.
fixIt.explain: A promise about the future: will + verb.

fixIt.text: He doesn't likes cold water.
fixIt.explain: After doesn't, no -s: he doesn't like.

fixIt.text: Every morning she drink a glass of milk.
fixIt.explain: Every morning is a habit, and she takes -s: she drinks.

fixIt.text: My parents has a small shop in the market.
fixIt.explain: Parents is they, so have, not has.

fixIt.text: I saw two mouse in the kitchen.
fixIt.explain: Mouse has an irregular plural: mice.

fixIt.text: We bought three kilo of mangoes.
fixIt.explain: Three means more than one: three kilos.

fixIt.text: These shoe are too small for me.
fixIt.explain: These + plural noun: these shoes.

fixIt.text: There is many people at the market.
fixIt.explain: People is plural: there are.

fixIt.text: Is this your brother phone?
fixIt.explain: The phone belongs to your brother: your brother's phone.

fixIt.text: The children toys are on the floor.
fixIt.explain: Children is already plural, so add 's: the children's toys.

fixIt.text: She is a honest person.
fixIt.explain: The h in honest is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound: an honest person.

fixIt.text: My sister is engineer at a factory.
fixIt.explain: Jobs need a or an, and engineer starts with a vowel sound: an engineer.

fixIt.text: I'm interested on history.
fixIt.explain: Interested in something.

fixIt.text: My birthday is in 15 May.
fixIt.explain: Dates take on: on 15 May.

fixIt.text: I go to work by foot.
fixIt.explain: On foot, but by bike, by bus, by car.

fixIt.text: What time you get up?
fixIt.explain: Present questions need do before the subject: What time do you get up?

fixIt.text: He is more taller than his father.
fixIt.explain: Taller is already a comparative. To make it stronger, use much: much taller.
